q: An attacker changes the 'price' field in an HTTP order request and pays 1 KM instead of 100 KM. Which STRIDE category?
explain: Data was modified in transit or on the client: that's tampering (integrity). Control: the server always calculates the price from its own data.

q: A user claims they didn't trigger a project deletion, and the application doesn't record who triggered the action. Which category?
explain: Repudiation is the ability to deny an action because there's no reliable evidence. Control: an audit log with identity, time and action, protected from modification.

q: An API returns a full stack trace with the database connection string when an error occurs. Which category?
explain: Leakage of sensitive information. Control: a generic message to the user, details only in the internal log.

q: A regular user can call /api/admin/users because the endpoint only checks that the user is logged in. Which category?
explain: The user gains rights that don't belong to them: that's elevation of privilege. Authentication is there, authorization is missing.

q: Where in a DFD do you most often look for threats?
options: On flows that cross trust boundaries
explain: At a trust boundary, data moves from a less trusted zone into a more trusted one (or vice versa). That's where authentication, validation and channel protection are needed.

q: Which STRIDE categories typically apply to a data FLOW? (multiple answers)
explain: A flow can be modified (T), eavesdropped on (I) or interrupted (D). A flow itself has no identity or privileges, so S and E aren't relevant to it.

q: What are the four threat modeling questions (Shostack)?
options: What are we working on? What can go wrong? What are we going to do about it? Did we do a good job?
explain: These four questions frame every threat modeling approach, regardless of tool or methodology.

q: A threat has been identified, but the system owner decides the cost of the control outweighs the risk. What is the right thing to do?
options: Ignore the threat and don't record it
Document the risk acceptance with a rationale and an owner
Delete the threat from the model
explain: Risk acceptance is a legitimate decision, but it must be conscious, recorded and owned, and revisited when circumstances change.

q: A fake internal service poses as the payment service because services don't verify each other's identity. Which control helps most directly?
options: mTLS or signed service tokens between services
explain: This is spoofing between services. mTLS (e.g. via a service mesh) or short-lived signed tokens give services a verifiable identity.

q: Which methodology specializes in PRIVACY threats?
explain: LINDDUN covers privacy threats (linkability, identifiability, non-repudiation, detectability, disclosure, unawareness, non-compliance).
